questions.text: In what John Carpenter classic is the following line said: 'I have come here to chew bubble gum and kick ass... and I'm all out of bubble gum'?
questions.funfact: The line was largely ad-libbed by wrestler-turned-actor Roddy Piper, inspired by pro wrestling promos he'd cut - it's since become one of the most quoted lines in action cinema.

questions.text: Who has just won the 2026 Women's US Open?
questions.funfact: Rybakina beat Sabalenka in New York to claim the 2026 US Open title, the same week Alexander Zverev won the men's singles.

questions.text: What does the word 'karaoke' translate to in English from Japanese?
questions.funfact: 'Kara' means 'empty' and 'oke' is a shortened form of 'okesutora' - a Japanese borrowing of the English word 'orchestra'.

questions.text: In the Tour de France, what jersey is given to the King of the Mountains?
questions.funfact: The polka dot jersey goes to the best climber, who collects points at summit finishes - the yellow jersey is the overall leader, green is the best sprinter, and white is the best rider aged 25 or under.

questions.text: Which female singer is an anagram of: LACROY SKELLKN
questions.funfact: Kelly Clarkson rose to fame as the first-ever winner of American Idol back in 2002.

questions.text: Which meat is used in the classic sandwich, a croque monsieur?
questions.funfact: A croque monsieur is a grilled ham and cheese sandwich topped with béchamel sauce - add a fried egg on top and it becomes a croque madame.

questions.text: What is Beyoncé's surname?
questions.funfact: Her full name is Beyoncé Giselle Knowles-Carter - Carter comes from her marriage to Jay-Z, whose real surname is also Carter.

questions.text: Where would you find the smallest bone in the human body?
questions.funfact: The stapes (stirrup), found in the middle ear, is the smallest bone in the body at just 2.5-3mm long. It's one of three tiny 'ossicles' - alongside the malleus (hammer) and incus (anvil) - that pass sound vibrations into the inner ear.

questions.text: Three of these flags are mostly red with one or more stars - which one doesn't fit that description?
questions.funfact: China, Morocco and Vietnam all have predominantly red flags featuring a star (or stars). Venezuela's flag is a yellow-blue-red tricolour with an arc of stars, so it's the odd one out.

questions.text: Guess the year: OpenAI was founded, 'See you again' by Charlie Puth was a huge hit, and Mad Max: Fury Road was released in cinemas.
questions.funfact: OpenAI was founded in December 2015, and Mad Max: Fury Road hit cinemas in May 2015.

questions.text: What does the DC stand for in Washington DC?
questions.funfact: The 'Columbia' part is a poetic, now largely retired name for the United States itself, honouring Christopher Columbus.

questions.text: Finish this old fashioned idiom or saying - 'Quit jivin' me…'
questions.funfact: 'Jivin'' here means kidding or fooling around, and 'turkey' has been American slang for a foolish or inept person since the mid-20th century.

questions.text: True or False: has evidence for liquid water ever been found on Mars?
questions.funfact: NASA announced on 28 September 2015 that data from the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter provided the strongest evidence yet for intermittent, present-day liquid salty brines flowing down warm Martian slopes.

questions.text: Where in the world was the original Kokoda Trail?
questions.funfact: The Kokoda Trail is a single-file track through the Owen Stanley Range, made famous by the brutal WWII campaign fought there between Australian and Japanese forces in 1942. It is 138km distance that is still completed today in memory of the trek veterans had previously completed

questions.text: Roald Dahl is known for his wonderful children's books, many of which have been adapted for TV and film. Name 5 of Roald Dahl's works that have been adapted for the big screen since the year 2000.
questions.funfact: Fantastic Mr. Fox (2009), Charlie and the Chocolate Factory (2005) and The BFG (2016) were all directed by different acclaimed filmmakers - Wes Anderson, Tim Burton and Steven Spielberg respectively.

questions.text: What do you call a sixty-fourth note in sheet music in Commonwealth countries?
questions.funfact: A quaver is an eighth note. Semi-, demi- and hemi- each mean 'half', so stacking them halves the value each time: semiquaver (1/16), demisemiquaver (1/32), and hemidemisemiquaver (1/64).

questions.text: Complete the next 5 lyrics: 'It's a little bit funny, this feeling inside / I'm not one of...'
questions.funfact: This is the opening line of Elton John's 'Your Song' (1970), written with lyricist Bernie Taupin - Elton has said he wrote the melody in under 20 minutes.

questions.text: What unusual shape is a goat's pupil?
questions.funfact: Goats (along with sheep and other grazing animals) have horizontal rectangular pupils, giving them a wide, panoramic field of view to spot predators while grazing with their heads down.

questions.text: What country is Kia from?
questions.funfact: Kia is South Korea's oldest surviving car manufacturer, founded in 1944 - it started out making steel tubing and bicycle parts before moving into motorcycles and eventually cars.

questions.text: Cerulean, Vermillion, Cinnabar, Carmine - one of these colours isn't a shade of red. Which one?
questions.funfact: Cerulean is a shade of sky blue - the other three are all deep shades of red.

questions.text: In chess notation, what letter is used to denote the Knight?
questions.funfact: N is used for the Knight because K is already taken by the King - every other piece (Q, R, B) uses its own first letter.

questions.text: What word can go before 'able' and 'mark', and after 'hand' and 'play', to make 4 new words?
questions.funfact: Bookable, bookmark, handbook and playbook.

questions.text: In Mario Kart, what do you call a small Koopa wearing goggles who stays airborne on a smiling white cloud and picks you up if you drop off the track?
questions.funfact: In Japan, Lakitu is called Jugem, a reference to a famous comic storytelling tale about a boy given an absurdly long name meaning 'limitless life'.

questions.text: Which is the older dinosaur: T-Rex or Stegosaurus?
questions.funfact: Stegosaurus lived during the late Jurassic period, roughly 150-155 million years ago, while T-Rex lived much later in the late Cretaceous, about 66-68 million years ago - T-Rex actually lived closer in time to us than to Stegosaurus.
questions.shoutout: 🎉 Shoutout to Henry for this question!

questions.text: What number can you remove 2 letters from to get a number that's one less, then remove 1 more letter to get back to the original number's value? (Hint: Think Roman Numerals!)
questions.funfact: FIVE, minus the F and E, leaves IV - the Roman numeral for 4, one less than 5. Remove the I from IV and you're left with just V - the Roman numeral for 5, back to the original value!

questions.text: In which of these political franchises is the famous line spoken: 'So this is how liberty dies... with thunderous applause'?
questions.funfact: The line is spoken by Padme Amidala (Natalie Portman) as she watches the Galactic Senate cheer the creation of the Empire - one of the most quoted lines in the entire Star Wars saga.

questions.text: What is the given name of China's current leader as of 2026 (Either First name or Last name)?
questions.funfact: In Chinese naming order the family name comes first, so 'Xi' is actually his surname and 'Jinping' is his given name - the reverse of Western naming order.

questions.text: Greece shares its national anthem with just one other country. Which country is it?
questions.funfact: Both countries use 'Hymn to Liberty' ('Ymnos is tin Eleftherian'), a 158-verse poem written by Dionysios Solomos in 1823, though only the first couple of verses are usually sung.

questions.text: What country did the festival of Diwali originate in?
questions.funfact: Diwali's roots trace back over 2,500 years to ancient India, believed to have started as a harvest festival before taking on the religious significance it holds today across Hinduism, Sikhism, Jainism, and Buddhism.

questions.text: Which movie is this anagram (ignore spaces): KRAIHOWTECOSENLT
questions.funfact: The Social Network (2010), dramatizes Facebook's founding and won three Oscars, including Best Adapted Screenplay for Aaron Sorkin. The upcoming sequel The Social Reckoning is coming out soon.

questions.text: Where is the flavourful food Pho famously from?
questions.funfact: Pho originated in northern Vietnam in the early 20th century and is often considered the country's unofficial national dish.

questions.text: North, Saint, Chicago and Psalm are the children of which celebrity couple? Name one of the parents.
questions.funfact: All four names were given by Kim Kardashian and Kanye West (now known as Ye) between 2013 and 2019.

questions.text: Carpal tunnel syndrome relates to which body part?
questions.funfact: It occurs when the median nerve, which runs through a narrow passage in the wrist, becomes compressed.

questions.text: Which of these countries does NOT have a capital city with the same name as the country?
questions.funfact: Mexico City, Panama City and Luxembourg (City) all share their country's name - Peru's capital, Lima, is the odd one out.

questions.text: Guess the year: Apple unveiled its first Macintosh computer, The Terminator hit cinemas, and Michael Jackson won 8 Grammys in a single night.
questions.funfact: Michael Jackson's record haul came at the 1984 Grammys for 'Thriller' - a record for a solo artist in one night that still stands.

questions.text: What does the 'D' stand for in BYD, the Chinese car manufacturer?
questions.funfact: BYD stands for 'Build Your Dreams' founded in 1995, it overtook Tesla in 2024 to become the world's best-selling EV maker by volume.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: 'Two shakes of a _____ tail.'
questions.funfact: The phrase means 'very quickly' - a lamb's tail wags fast, giving us this bit of old farmyard slang.

questions.text: Which city are the Red Sox baseball team famously from?
questions.funfact: The Red Sox have played at Boston's Fenway Park, the oldest ballpark still in use in Major League Baseball, since 1912.

questions.text: Which actor stars in the upcoming movie 'Digger', playing the titular character?
questions.funfact: Digger (2026) is directed by Alejandro G. Inarritu - his first film since 2015's The Revenant.

questions.text: Name Fleetwood Mac's top 5 most-streamed songs on Spotify, in any order.
questions.funfact: 'Dreams' alone has racked up nearly 3 billion Spotify streams, helped by a huge resurgence when a viral 2020 TikTok video sent it back up the charts decades after release.

questions.text: What is the name of Coldplay's first album?
options: A Rush of Blood to the Head
questions.funfact: Parachutes was released in 2000 and includes the breakout hit single 'Yellow'.

questions.text: Complete the next 5 lyrics: 'Never gonna give you up / Never gonna let you down / Never gonna...'
questions.funfact: This is Rick Astley's 1987 hit 'Never Gonna Give You Up', the song behind the internet meme 'Rickrolling'.

questions.text: What is a baby goose called?
questions.funfact: Goslings typically stay close to their parents for the first two to three months before they can fly.

questions.text: Famous for its plaid check pattern, what is the name of this British luxury brand?
questions.funfact: Burberry's iconic check was originally used as a lining for trench coats in the 1920s before becoming a signature design element in its own right.

questions.text: Which of these is the odd one out?
questions.funfact: IKEA (Ingvar Kamprad Elmtaryd Agunnaryd), RADAR (RAdio Detection And Ranging) and LASER (Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation) are all genuine acronyms - Xerox is not, it comes from 'xerography', the dry-printing process the company was named after.

questions.text: What is the only word in the English language that has three double letters in a row?
questions.funfact: Break it down: boo-kk-ee-per - the double O, double K and double E sit back-to-back, making 'bookkeeper' (and 'bookkeeping') a genuine linguistic oddity.

questions.text: What is the name given to the little blob of toothpaste you put on your toothbrush?
questions.funfact: The term 'nurdle' became the subject of a real trademark lawsuit in 2010 between GSK and Colgate-Palmolive over its use in advertising.

questions.text: Originally recorded by Lori Lieberman in 1971, the song 'Killing Me Softly with His Song' was inspired by which music artist's performance?
questions.funfact: Lieberman was reportedly moved after seeing Don McLean perform 'Empty Chairs' live in Los Angeles - the song was later made famous by Roberta Flack in 1973 and the Fugees in 1996.

questions.text: '_____ dogs' refers to the famous animal subjects used in a series of 1897 experiments that led to the discovery of classical conditioning. What is the name of the Russian physiologist behind these experiments?
questions.funfact: Pavlov noticed his dogs salivating at the sound of a bell alone, once they'd learned to associate it with food, the foundation of what we now call 'Pavlovian' or classical conditioning.
questions.shoutout: 🎉 Shoutout to James for this question!

questions.text: What is the maximum number of Friday the 13ths that can happen in a single calendar year?
questions.funfact: It last happened in 2015, when February, March and November all opened on a Friday the 13th, as February has 28 days, excluding Leap Years, if there is a friday 13th in February there will be another in March too, leading to 3 in a given year.

questions.text: In which of these 90's classics is the line spoken: 'In case I don't see you, good afternoon, good evening, good night!'?
questions.funfact: The line is Truman Burbank's signature sign-off, said throughout the show-within-the-show - fittingly used again as his final line when he walks off set at the end of the film.

questions.text: Which Premier League club has just been found guilty of all 115 charges of breaching financial rules over a 9-year period between 2009 and 2018?
questions.funfact: The charges covered alleged breaches from the 2009-10 season through to 2017-18, spanning financial fair play rules, profitability requirements, and failing to cooperate with the Premier League's investigation.

questions.text: Translated as 'the little boy' in Spanish, what is the name given to the natural climate pattern that increases warm ocean currents in the Pacific Ocean?
questions.funfact: Combined with long-term climate trends, this super El Nino has driven global ocean temperatures to historic highs, putting 2027 on track to potentially become the hottest year on record.

questions.text: The Gobi Desert stretches over China and which other country?
questions.funfact: The Gobi is Asia's largest desert, spanning roughly 1.3 million square kilometres across southern Mongolia and northern China.

questions.text: Where does a troglodyte live?
questions.funfact: The word comes from the Greek 'troglodytes', meaning 'one who creeps into holes' - historically used to describe cave-dwelling peoples.

questions.text: Where do pierogies traditionally come from?
questions.funfact: Pierogi have been a staple of Polish cuisine since the Middle Ages, though neighbouring Ukraine, Russia and Slovakia all have their own versions and some claim to the dish's origins too.

questions.text: Which celebrity is famous for the brand Fenty?
questions.funfact: Rihanna launched Fenty Beauty in 2017 with an unprecedented 40 foundation shades, widely credited with pushing the beauty industry toward better shade inclusivity.

questions.text: Where would you find your thyroid in the body?
questions.funfact: The thyroid is a butterfly-shaped gland at the base of the neck that regulates metabolism by producing hormones

questions.text: What is the capital of Scotland?
questions.funfact: Despite Glasgow being Scotland's largest city, Edinburgh has been the capital since at least the 15th century and is home to the Scottish Parliament.

questions.text: Guess the year: Malala Yousafzai became the youngest-ever Nobel Peace Prize laureate, How I Met Your Mother aired its finale, and Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 mysteriously vanished over the Indian Ocean.
questions.funfact: Malala Yousafzai won the Nobel Peace Prize at just 17 years old, sharing it with Indian children's rights activist Kailash Satyarthi.

questions.text: RSPCA - what does the C stand for?
questions.funfact: The RSPCA stands for the Royal Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals

questions.text: In Gen Z slang, what does 'cooked' mean?
questions.funfact: 'Cooked' exploded in Gen Z slang via gaming and TikTok culture, meaning someone is finished, doomed, or about to fail spectacularly. For example 'bro is cooked' after a bad test.

questions.text: Which of the following TV shows had the most episodes?
questions.funfact: Friends ran for 10 seasons and 236 episodes, well ahead of The US Office's 201 (9 seasons), Seinfeld's 180 (9 seasons), and Parks and Recreation's 125 (7 seasons).

questions.text: The 2026 movie 'Tony' that has just been released is a biopic about which famous person? (Full name)
questions.funfact: Tony stars Dominic Sessa as the late chef, author and TV host, showing his experiences before writing his acclaimed Kitchen Confidential.

questions.text: Hydrogen and Helium are the first 2 elements of the Periodic Table, name the next 5 elements. (Hint: Initials are L, B, B, C, N)
questions.funfact: Lithium through Nitrogen make up elements 3 through 7 on the periodic table. Lithium is prized for batteries, while Nitrogen makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere.

questions.text: What is the name of Taylor Swift's latest single, released last week, that shares its name with the technical term for the very first individual to contract a specific disease?
questions.funfact: The term is believed to stem from a mislabeling during 1980s AIDS research, when a Canadian flight attendant was labelled Patient 'O' (for 'Outside California') - later misread as the number zero.

questions.text: Complete the next 4 lyrics: 'Someday I'll wish upon a star / And wake up where the clouds are far behind me / Where troubles melt like lemon drops / Away...'
questions.funfact: This is 'Over the Rainbow' from The Wizard of Oz. It won the Academy Award for Best Original Song in 1939 and was later named the greatest movie song of all time by the American Film Institute.

questions.text: What is the name given to a squirrel's den?
questions.funfact: A drey is typically built high in tree forks from twigs, leaves and bark, and squirrels often maintain multiple dreys across their territory.

questions.text: Which of these is the biggest selling coffee brand by sales in the world?
questions.funfact: Nescafe's footprint is so vast that one out of every seven cups of coffee consumed worldwide is a Nescafé product

questions.text: Three of these are short pasta shapes - which one is the odd one out?
questions.funfact: Stracciatella is the Burrata Filling, the creamy, gooey center that spills out when you cut open a ball of burrata. Bucatini is a long, thick noodle with a hollow centre running through it like a straw. Farfalle is bow-tie shaped pasta. Orecchiette means 'little ears' in Italian.

questions.text: Trypophobia is a fear of what?
options: Clusters of small holes or bumps
questions.funfact: Though not officially recognised as a clinical phobia, trypophobia sufferers report real feelings of disgust or unease when viewing clustered holes like lotus seed pods or honeycomb.

questions.text: Which country's name is spelled using the 7 most common letters in the English alphabet, once each?
questions.funfact: The most frequently used letters in English are roughly E, T, A, O, I, N, S - rearranged, they spell 'Estonia'

questions.text: What is the scientific or medical term for 'goosebumps'?
questions.funfact: All three terms describe the same reflex: tiny muscles at the base of hair follicles contracting, a leftover survival response from when our ancestors had enough body hair for it to trap warmth or make them look bigger to predators.

questions.text: Which of the following foods is Kosher?
questions.funfact: Kosher dietary law permits mammals that both chew cud and have cloven hooves (like goats and cows), while pork and shellfish are both forbidden - most insects, including crickets, are non-kosher too, with only a few specific locust species as an exception.
questions.shoutout: 🎉 Shoutout to Talisia for this question!

questions.text: On a standard Rubik's Cube, how many small cubes can you actually see and touch on the outside of the cube?
questions.funfact: A Rubik's Cube has 27 small cubes total (3x3x3), but the very centre cube is completely hidden inside the mechanism with no stickers at all - leaving 26 you can see and touch: 8 corners, 12 edges, and 6 face centres.
